checks.text: All external bleeding stopped within 2 minutes
checks.why: The right arm still bleeds; the left is held by the tourniquet. Dress both so the tourniquet can come off later.

checks.text: IV or IO access within 2 minutes
checks.why: Arm IVs fail below a systolic of 70 and damaged limbs lower the chance further; an IO always succeeds.

checks.text: Dog tag checked before the first blood bag
checks.why: The kit holds A+, B- and O- blood. Only the blood type on the dog tag tells you which bags he can take.
A B- casualty can only receive B- or O-. Incompatible blood causes a hemolytic reaction and only counts as saline.
Blood restores oxygen-carrying volume; saline only converts slowly.

checks.text: Pain treated with an opioid or ketamine
checks.why: He is awake with two arm wounds and a tourniquet. A full weight-based dose (about 8 mg morphine IV for him) controls the pain.
Opioid doses add up: morphine IV overdoses above 12 mg active (with up to 3 mg of variation). Wait for one dose to act before giving more.

checks.text: Blood volume at least 5.1 L at the end
checks.why: Two compatible units bring him back above 5.1 L, where he can wake up.
